correctness.rationale: For any input state, the amplitude-damping output determinant splits into the pure-state value \(p(1-p)q^2\) plus the nonnegative mixedness term \((1-p)(q(1-q)-|z|^2)\), and qubit entropy is strictly increasing with determinant. The source proves the unique optimal average \(\tau_*\) and the fixed-input roof \(g_p\); strict convexity of \(g_p\) forces equality in Jensen only when every signal excitation equals \(q_*\). Output-entropy equality then forces every signal pure. The average coherence is exactly \(\sqrt{q_*(1-q_*)}\) times the weighted phasor sum, yielding the iff phase-balance condition. The polygon criterion gives the exact probability-vector condition. Endpoint and generalized-channel cases are excluded.

value.rationale: The result is a natural complete classification attached to a newly settled operational capacity problem: it identifies every exact capacity-achieving finite signal alphabet, not merely one optimizer. The probability-simplex criterion \(\max_j\pi_j\le 1/2\) and support-minimal uniqueness tell exactly which priors can be used without rate loss and distinguish essential structure from the previously known regular-polygon examples. This is a structural equality theorem, not a parameter substitution or numerical recomputation.
